protocol.py: 4 biology problems (3 errors, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 15 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 46:  p300.mix(2, 15, plate[well])
   At line 46 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 15 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 16 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [e905b2270bad]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 3: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 46:  p300.mix(2, 15, plate[well])
   At line 46 the p300_single_gen2 draws 15 ul from well A1 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm
   above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 20 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well
   Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.63 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 16 times; 240 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does
   not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not
   mixed. Source wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [61972b459fc3]

3. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 3: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 57:  p20.mix(2, 10, plate[dst])
   At line 57 the p20_single_gen2 draws 10 ul from well A1 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm above
   the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 25 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate
   200 µL Flat reaches only 0.79 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line
   did it 14 times; 140 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow
   the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed.
   Source wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [cba132b7800f]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 7 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and
3 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 55:  p20.dispense(5, plate[dst])
   At line 55 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 3 more to wells A1,
   B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3, which already held master mix (this line did it 7
   times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run
   ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so
   what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually
   vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3 after line 55: `mix_after=(5, 20)`
   on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the
   well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [9a4a1ff5745c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.explanation: At line 46 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 15 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 16 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 3: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 46 the p300_single_gen2 draws 15 ul from well A1 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 20 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.63 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 16 times; 240 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed. Source wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and H1 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.

By then the well holds 25 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.79 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 14 times; 140 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed. Source wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3.

findings.title: 7 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 3 more went in (20% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 55 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 3 more to wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3, which already held master mix (this line did it 7 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 3 after line 55: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
